# contrast.plot_contrasts.plot_contrasts { #fmrimod.contrast.plot_contrasts.plot_contrasts }

```python
plot_contrasts(
    x,
    absolute_limits=False,
    rotate_x_text=True,
    scale_mode='auto',
    figsize=None,
    cmap=None,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Plot contrast weights as a heatmap.

This is a generic function that dispatches based on the type of x.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                         | Description                                                     | Default    |
|-----------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| x               | object                       | Object containing contrast information (EventModel, dict, etc.) | _required_ |
| absolute_limits | bool                         | If True, fix color scale at (-1, 1). If False, use data range.  | `False`    |
| rotate_x_text   | bool                         | If True, rotate x-axis labels for readability.                  | `True`     |
| scale_mode      | (auto, diverging, one_sided) | Color scale mode. 'auto' chooses based on data.                 | `'auto'`   |
| figsize         | tuple                        | Figure size (width, height)                                     | `None`     |
| cmap            | str                          | Colormap name. If None, chosen based on scale_mode.             | `None`     |
| **kwargs        | object                       | Additional arguments passed to plotting functions               | `{}`       |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description       |
|--------|--------------------------|-------------------|
|        | matplotlib.figure.Figure | The figure object |
